function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

message.content:
Below is a quick‑look guide to the **next few high‑profile U.S. festivals** that you’ll find happening over the coming months.  
(If you’re looking for something more niche—food fairs, film festivals, regional celebrations, or specific city line‑ups—just let me know!)

| # | Festival | Dates 2026 | Location | What’s Special |
|---|----------|------------|-----------|----------------|
| 1 | **South By Southwest (SXSW)** | **March 11–20** | Austin, Texas | World‑class mix of music, film, interactive media, and tech talks. Expect headline acts plus indie gems. |
| 2 | **Coachella Valley Music & Arts Festival** | **April 8–9** | Indio, California (Empire Polo Club) | Iconic two‑day pop‑culture event featuring top rock, hip‑hop, electronic artists + art installations. |
| 3 | **Bonnaroo Music & Arts Festival** | **June 15–18** | Manchester, Tennessee | Three days of eclectic music across multiple stages, food trucks, arts workshops, and a “bunny” mascot parade. |
| 4 | **Burning Man** | **August 27–September 5** | Black Rock Desert, Nevada | Radical self‑expression meets community building. Prepare for extreme desert conditions and elaborate art structures. |
| 5 | **New Orleans Jazz & Heritage Festival** | **May 26–29** | New Orleans, Louisiana | Celebrates jazz, blues, zydeco, world music, and Southern cuisine. Great street parades and live performances. |

### Quick Tips Before You Go

| Tip | Why It Matters |
|-----|----------------|
| **Book Early** | Tickets sell out fast—especially for SXSW and Coachella. |
| **Plan Transportation** | Many venues are remote; consider carpool apps or shuttle services. |
| **Pack Appropriately** | Weather varies widely—from hot desert heat at Coachella to humid summer in Nashville. |
| **Check COVID‑19 Guidelines** | Some festivals still require proof of vaccination or mask policies. |
| **Explore Local Food** | Festivals often feature unique culinary stalls—don’t miss them! |

---

#### Want More Details?

* Line‑up announcements (usually late January / February)
* Accommodation options near each venue
* Volunteer opportunities
* Family‑friendly activities

Just drop a follow‑up note and I’ll dig deeper into whatever aspect interests you most!
